chapter: Pedal points, Hampton, Norvo and Debut
title: Blind Tom and whether Erroll Garner could read
summary: Memory pianists; Mingus disputes that Garner could not read, citing Garner's brother.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, I would agree with that.

Blind Tom, he say he can go to Europe A Symphony for him, and and play his own band (unintelligible) he can sit down and play at home. That's pretty good. I couldn't do that. That's (unintelligible) a whole lot of memory in it.

Well, yeah, Erroll Garner -- Martha Glaser told me he went to a concert in Carnegie Hall and went back upstairs, and his studio is upstairs, in Carnegie Hall (inaudible) upstairs, and sat down and played a whole piece through, because he remembered it. But that's how he learned, he couldn't read, he couldn't --
* 19th-Century pianist, born a slave, blind from birth, Viz: Eileen Southern, The Music of Black Americans; Langston Hughes, Black Magic.
HEMLOCK
Erroll Garner couldn't read, who told you that?
(Inaudible.)
Well, Martha's his manager.
She's full of shit.
Oh, yeah?

Erroll Garner and his brother both played piano, and they studied classical piano. I worked with Timmie Rogers when Erroll Garner's brother was on it. I said, 'Man, how come you can read so well, man?' (Inaudible) Martha Gleason told Erroll that everybody thinks it's best for a black man who can't read -- to say he can't read, and it just comes from the heart and the soul. Born in a black man's soul." And when he began to act it out. that's (inaudible). I'm not saying he's no sight reader, but his brother was a sight reader.
Was that Winton?

Yeah, piano player. I just saw him; last time I was in Canada (Inaudible) he came by. We was talking about that, about Erroll saying he couldn't read. Now, everybody thinks it's how he can't read. better that the black man plays the piano (inaudible). Ask his brother.
I never met his brother. I just know Martha.
Well, she -- maybe she didn't know.
Maybe she didn't.
he had such a good ear
Errol just probably didn't -- (inaudible) that he didn't need to read. He made his own tunes up all day
HEMLOCK FRASABLE COTTON CONTENT
He was a spontaneous composer.
